papers.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
papers.abstract: VFlash predicts structured visual primitives such as points, boxes and variable-length trajectories jointly in one forward pass instead of autoregressively decoding coordinate tokens. Its authors report approximately 25× faster single-rollout generation for 3D point-motion forecasting and improved downstream WAM planning results.
papers.contribution: Primitive-aware flash decoding for structured spatial outputs, with type-, dimension- and length-adaptive layouts.
papers.limitations: Fast plan decoding does not by itself guarantee kinematic feasibility or closed-loop physical correctness. Validate end-to-end latency and physical execution separately.
embodiments: robot trajectory planning; specific hardware should be confirmed
papers.real_robot: Not established from the abstract inspected.

papers.title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling
papers.authors: Mateo Clémente, George Z. Xue, Amin Abyaneh, Liheng Ma, Rui Heng Yang, Tongtong Cao, Zhanguang Zhang, Yingxue Zhang
papers.abstract: A compact world-action model trained from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder. It predicts future features jointly with actions during training and generates only actions at inference. The paper reports strong RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO-Plus results and comparable performance to π0.5 on four real-robot tasks.
papers.contribution: Control-oriented latent world-action policy; contrasts JEPA features with video VAE latents and studies training-time future prediction choices.
papers.limitations: New preprint; results and baseline comparisons need independent reproduction. Verify benchmark instruction corrections and hardware conditions before drawing conclusions.
embodiments: robot manipulation; exact hardware variants should be checked in full text
papers.real_robot: Yes — four real-robot tasks are stated in the abstract.
papers.notes: Seeded from the 5 Nov 2026 arXiv record. Metadata and claims should be refreshed by the automated ingestion pipeline.

papers.title: World-Action Models for Robot Learning and Control: A Survey
papers.abstract: A robotics-oriented survey of world-action models covering representations, transition modelling, action interfaces, architectures, training pipelines, data modalities, scaling, benchmarks and challenges.
papers.contribution: Connects WAM research with manipulation, navigation and autonomous driving, and identifies issues such as action alignment, spatial consistency, memory and efficient inference.
papers.limitations: Survey scope and completeness are constrained by its date; compare with newer submissions and project releases.

papers.title: World Action Models: The Next Frontier in Embodied AI
papers.abstract: A survey defining World-Action Models as embodied foundation models coupling predictive state modelling with executable action generation. It organizes WAMs into cascaded and joint architectures and reviews data, evaluation and open challenges.
papers.contribution: Provides a conceptual framework distinguishing WAMs from reactive VLA policies, conventional world models and action-conditioned video generation.
papers.limitations: A survey reflects its publication cutoff; use it as a taxonomy and verify later papers independently.

papers.title: π₀: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
papers.abstract: Introduces a generalist robot policy that combines a pretrained vision-language model with a flow-matching action expert to generate continuous robot action chunks across multiple tasks and embodiments.
papers.contribution: Flow-matching action generation as an alternative to discrete autoregressive action tokenization.
papers.limitations: Generative action inference can be computationally expensive; deployment latency, embodiment coverage and fine-grained control remain important evaluation dimensions.
datasets: large multi-robot demonstration data; see paper for exact mixture
papers.real_robot: Yes — physical robot evaluations are reported.

papers.title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model
papers.abstract: An open-source 7B vision-language-action model based on a pretrained vision-language backbone and trained on a large multi-robot demonstration corpus. It provides an accessible baseline for adaptation and evaluation.
papers.contribution: Open, reproducible VLA foundation model with released weights and fine-tuning code.
papers.limitations: Autoregressive tokenized actions, dataset coverage and deployment compute are important constraints; performance depends on fine-tuning and embodiment compatibility.
embodiments: multiple robot arms represented in training mixture
papers.real_robot: Yes — physical robot evaluations are reported in the paper.

papers.title: Octo: An Open-Source Generalist Robot Policy
papers.abstract: A transformer-based generalist robot policy trained on a diverse mixture of robot trajectories and designed to be fine-tuned for new observation and action spaces.
papers.contribution: Open generalist policy and training recipe for adapting across robot setups.
papers.limitations: Generalization still depends on the training mixture and downstream adaptation; action spaces and observations need careful alignment.
papers.real_robot: Yes — real-world fine-tuning and evaluation are reported.

papers.title: 3D-VLA: A 3D Vision-Language-Action Generative World Model
papers.abstract: Combines 3D perception, language-conditioned reasoning and generative world modelling for embodied tasks, emphasizing spatially grounded interaction.
papers.contribution: Connects 3D scene understanding with language-conditioned action and generative world modelling.
papers.limitations: Check the full experimental setup when comparing simulated results to physical robot performance; 3D representation quality is a major dependency.
papers.real_robot: Not assumed; verify full paper before claiming physical deployment.

papers.title: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models
papers.abstract: A standardized multi-robot dataset and RT-X model effort assembled from 22 robot embodiments and 21 institutions, spanning 527 skills and 160,266 tasks. The authors demonstrate positive transfer across robot platforms.
papers.contribution: A foundational data infrastructure for X-robot policy learning and cross-embodiment transfer.
papers.limitations: Dataset heterogeneity, embodiment alignment and task-distribution coverage remain important constraints; aggregate scale does not guarantee uniform quality across all tasks.
papers.real_robot: Yes — dataset and experiments comprise real robot data.
papers.notes: First submitted 13 Oct 2023; peer-reviewed ICRA 2024 publication. Bibliographic details verified against arXiv and ICRA publication metadata.

papers.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
papers.abstract: A vision-language-action approach that co-fine-tunes vision-language models on web-scale vision-language data and robot demonstrations, representing robot actions as token sequences.
papers.contribution: Demonstrates transfer of semantic knowledge from web pretraining into robotic manipulation.
papers.limitations: Action tokenization and limited robot data coverage; strong semantic performance is not equivalent to broad physical competence.
papers.real_robot: Yes — physical robot experiments are reported.

papers.title: PaLM-E: An Embodied Multimodal Language Model
papers.abstract: An embodied multimodal language model that integrates continuous observations such as images and state estimates into a language model for robotics and multimodal reasoning tasks.
papers.contribution: A unified multimodal language-model approach that accepts embodied observations and transfers across language, vision and robotics tasks.
papers.limitations: A model capable of embodied reasoning is not necessarily a high-frequency low-level controller; closed-loop execution requires separate control machinery.
datasets: robotics and multimodal task datasets; see paper
papers.real_robot: Yes — real robotic tasks are included.

papers.title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
papers.abstract: Combines language-model task proposals with learned robotic affordance values to select executable skills and ground open-ended instructions in physical capabilities.
papers.contribution: A foundational neuro-symbolic planning architecture connecting semantic intent to low-level skill feasibility.
papers.limitations: Depends on the available skill library and affordance estimates; novel skills require separate learning or composition.
papers.real_robot: Yes — physical robot demonstrations and evaluations are reported.
